pairs: if you have taken a pledge on behalf of your friend,
then you have bound your hand to an outsider,
then you are ensnared by the words of your own mouth,
and taken captive by your own words.
do what I say, and free yourself,
quia incidisti in manum proximi tui. Discurre,
for you have fallen into the hand of your neighbor.
Do not grant sleep to your eyes,
Rescue yourself like a gazelle from the hand,
et quasi avis de manu aucupis.
and like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
For though she has no ruler,
she provides meals for herself in the summer,
et congregat in messe quod comedat.
and she gathers at the harvest what she may eat.
When will you rise up from your sleep?
you will fold your hands a little to sleep,
et veniet tibi quasi viator egestas,
and then destitution will meet with you, like a traveler,
and poverty, like an armed man. Yet truly,
Si vero impiger fueris, veniet ut fons messis tua,
if you would be diligent, then your harvest will arrive like a fountain,
et egestas longe fugiet a te.
and destitution will flee far from you.
With a depraved heart he devises evil,
and at all times he sows conflict.
To this one, his perdition will arrive promptly,
and he shall be crushed suddenly:
he will no longer have any remedy.
Six things there are that the Lord hates,
and the seventh, his soul detests:
a heart that devises the most wicked thoughts,
pedes veloces ad currendum in malum,
a deceitful witness bringing forth lies,
et eum qui seminat inter fratres discordias.
and he who sows discord among brothers.
preserve the precepts of your father,
et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ.
and do not dismiss the law of your mother.
Liga ea in corde tuo jugiter,
Bind them to your heart unceasingly,
and encircle them around your throat.
When you walk, let them keep step with you.
And when you keep watch, speak with them.
and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life.
ut custodiant te a muliere mala,
So may they guard you from an evil woman,
and from the flattering tongue of the outsider.
Non concupiscat pulchritudinem ejus cor tuum,
Let not your heart desire her beauty;
do not be captivated by her winks.
pretium enim scorti vix est unius panis,
For the price of a prostitute is only one loaf.
mulier autem viri pretiosam animam capit.
Yet the woman seizes the precious soul of a man.
Numquid potest homo abscondere ignem in sinu suo,
Would a man be able to conceal fire in his bosom,
so that his garments would not burn?
Or could he walk over burning coals,
so that his feet would not be burned?
sic qui ingreditur ad mulierem proximi sui,
non erit mundus cum tetigerit eam.
he who enters to the wife of his neighbor shall not be clean when he touches her.
Non grandis est culpa cum quis furatus fuerit:
Not so great is the fault when someone has stolen.
furatur enim ut esurientem impleat animam;
For he steals so as to satisfy a hungry soul.
et omnem substantiam domus suæ tradet.
he shall repay sevenfold and hand over all the substance of his house.
propter cordis inopiam perdet animam suam;
because of the emptiness of his heart, will destroy his own soul.
He gathers shame and dishonor to himself,
and his disgrace will not be wiped away.
quia zelus et furor viri non parcet in die vindictæ,
For the jealousy and fury of the husband will not spare him on the day of vindication,
nor will he agree to the pleadings of anyone,
nec suscipiet pro redemptione dona plurima.
nor will he accept, as repayment, a multitude of gifts.
